on that entire distant cone. Both sides are doubly periodic. Their common period lattice $L$ has finite index. Choose a nonzero $q\in L$ with direction strictly inside $K'$; such a vector exists by density of rational directions and finite index. For any lattice point $z_0$, $z_0+nq$ enters the distant cone for all sufficiently large $n$. Hence $b-b_K$ vanishes on every $L$-coset and therefore everywhere. Thus $b=b_K$, which is preserved by every original $H_i$. This uses one realized sector, with no sector-adjacency cycle or color-background gluing.

### 3.4. No direction can be missing

Since $D\in\varphi\mathcal H$, $\varphi\mid D$. In characteristic zero,
$$
D=\prod_i\prod_{\lambda^{\kappa_i}=1}(T^{v_i}-\lambda).
$$
Each binomial is prime: completing primitive $v_i$ to a lattice basis makes its quotient a one-variable Laurent domain. Distinct roots and nonparallel directions give nonassociate primes, so $D$ is squarefree. Therefore $\varphi$ has the stated grouped form, initially allowing $A_i'=1$.

If direction $i$ were missing, $\varphi\mid Q_i$ and $f_i=(Q_i/\varphi)b$ would be doubly periodic. But a nonzero doubly periodic function cannot be supported in a finite-width strip: its period lattice contains a vector with nonzero $\pi_i$-projection, whose multiples carry any nonzero point out of the strip. This contradicts Section 3.1. Thus every $d_i'\ge1$. Newton additivity gives $Z'$, with nonempty interior since at least two directions are nonparallel.

### 3.5. Affine divisibility

If $f\eta=c$ is constant, then both $(T^{e_1}-1)f$ and $(T^{e_2}-1)f$ annihilate $\eta$, hence are divisible by $\varphi$. The coordinate binomials are coprime. Each prime factor of $\varphi$ therefore divides $f$; squarefreeness gives $\varphi\mid f$. The zero polynomial case is immediate. This treats the constant term without asserting that $f$ itself annihilates $\eta$, and completes the bridge.

## 4. The rewritten affine budget (CN Lemma 2.5)

For nonempty finite $S=\operatorname{Conv}(S)\cap\mathbb Z^2$, let $\mathcal L_S$ be the full pattern set and put
$$
E=\{r\in\mathbb Z^2:r+Z'\subseteq\operatorname{Conv}(S)\},\qquad
U_S=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{1,\gamma\mapsto w(\gamma(s)):s\in S\}.
$$
The relation space of $(c_0,f)$ with $\operatorname{supp}f\subseteq S$, $f\eta=c_0$ has unchanged dimension over $\mathbb C$: the integer system has finitely many unknowns, hence a finite row basis despite infinitely many anchors. A nonzero relation has $f\ne0$; the bridge gives $f=\varphi g$. Newton additivity implies $Z'+\operatorname{Newt}(g)\subseteq\operatorname{Conv}(S)$, so $\operatorname{supp}g\subseteq E$. The linear map $(c_0,f)\mapsto g$ is injective, giving
$$
\dim_{\mathbb Q}U_S\ge |S|+1-|E|.
$$
This uses only an injection of relation spaces, valid also for $b\ne0$. Since $0\in Z'$, $E$ is finite. Empty $E$ proves the bound immediately, including point and segment windows because $Z'$ is two-dimensional.

## 5. The witness and rewritten Lemma 5.1

CN Lemma 4.2 now applies using Section 3.1: $J(d,z):=D_z[\eta(z)\eta(z+d)]$ has finite support for every $d$, and is nonzero for some $d$. Its nonvanishing proof uses two nonparallel nonzero strips, their nonzero finite-support product, and Lemma 1.2; it has no spectral input.

Write $T_d^sJ(d,z)=J(d+s,z)$, $T_z^sJ(d,z)=J(d,z+s)$. The new bi-recursion is
$$
\varphi(T_d)J=D_z[\eta(z)b(z+d)]=b(z+d)D\eta(z)=0,
$$
$$
\varphi(T_zT_d^{-1})J=D_z[b(z)\eta(z+d)]=b(z)D\eta(z+d)=0.
$$
The first applies $\varphi$ to the second observation point. For the second, $(d,z)\mapsto(d-s,z+s)$ moves only the first. In each formal subset expansion of $D$, every $H_C$ preserves $b$, allowing it to factor out. These identities hold for nonzero $b$ as well.

## 6. Checking the new-parameter localization

For CN Lemma 5.2, put $K=\mathbb C(X_1,X_2)$, $B=K[Y_1^{\pm1},Y_2^{\pm1}]$ and
$$
a_i=A_i'(Y^{v_i}),\quad c_i=A_i'(X^{v_i}Y^{-v_i}),\quad a=\varphi(Y),\quad c=\varphi(X/Y).
$$
Over the algebraic closure of $K$, $a_i=c_i=0$ would force $X^{v_i}=\lambda\mu\in\mathbb C$, impossible. Two nonparallel $a$-factors vanishing force both $Y$ coordinates to be algebraic over $\mathbb C$, hence in $\mathbb C^\times$, excluding every $c$-factor. Applied to $X/Y$, the same argument excludes simultaneous vanishing of two distinct $c$-factors and any $a$-factor. Thus Nullstellensatz and faithful flatness give both CRT steps:
$$
B/(a,c)\simeq\prod_{i\ne j}B/(a_i,c_j).
$$
First split the pairwise comaximal $a_i$ modulo $c$; modulo $a_i$, $c_i$ is a unit and the remaining $c_j$ are pairwise comaximal. Only nonzero complex roots and nonparallel directions were required.

For factor $(i,j)$, take all $|\det(v_i,v_j)|$ lattice representatives $r_n$ in $\{\alpha v_i-\beta v_j:0\le\alpha,\beta<1\}$. The Laurent ring is free on $Y^{r_n}$ over the subring in $Y^{v_i},Y^{-v_j}$. Nonzero end coefficients reduce all positive and negative powers, giving spanning exponents
$$
r_n+sv_i-tv_j\in[0,d_i'v_i]+[0,-d_j'v_j],\qquad 0\le s<d_i',\quad0\le t<d_j'.
$$
All representatives are kept even for nonunimodular pairs. CN's $E_{ij}=\prod_{k\ne i}a_k\prod_{l\ne j}c_l$ is invertible in factor $(i,j)$ and zero elsewhere, by the same no-common-zero checks. For all the reduced exponents above,
$$
\operatorname{supp}(E_{ij})+(r_n+sv_i-tv_j)\subseteq Z'-Z'.
$$
The products $E_{ij}Y^{r_n+sv_i-tv_j}$ span factor $(i,j)$ and vanish in every other factor, proving the new spanning statement.

For Proposition 5.3, define the $K$-linear functional
$$
L(Y^d)=\widehat J(d;X):=\sum_zJ(d,z)X^{-z}.
$$
Finite support makes this an element of $K$. The recursions give $L(Y^da)=L(Y^dc)=0$ for every $d$: shifting $z$ by $s$ contributes $X^s$, matching $\varphi(X/Y)$. $K$-linearity kills the entire ideal. If all $J$ on $Z'-Z'$ vanished, the spanning statement would force $L=0$, contradicting the nonzero witness. The localized displacement is nonzero since $J(0,z)=D\eta^2=0$, which uses full color Case B.

## 7. Closing Theorem T

CN Lemma 6.1 applies to the two-dimensional lattice zonotope $Z'$ and gives
$$
(Z'-Z')\cap\mathbb Z^2=(Z'\cap\mathbb Z^2)-(Z'\cap\mathbb Z^2).
$$
Its proof uses central symmetry and a unimodular triangulation of the polygon; no direction pair must be unimodular. Thus write the new witness $d=q_1-q_0$ with both $q_i$ in $Z'\cap\mathbb Z^2$. For $r\in E$, lattice convexity gives $r+q_0,r+q_1\in S$. Define
$$
\Phi_r(\gamma)=w(\gamma(r+q_0))w(\gamma(r+q_1)).
$$
As in CN Lemma 7.2, a nontrivial relation $\sum_rc_r\Phi_r\in U_S$, evaluated at all anchors and differenced by $D$, would give
$$
\left(\sum_rc_rT^{r+q_0}\right)J(d,\cdot)=0,
$$
contradicting Lemma 1.2. Hence
$$
P_\theta(S)\ge\dim U_S+|E|\ge|S|+1.
$$
The same new erosion supplies deficit and capacity. Together with Case A this proves the original Theorem T for all nonempty finite lattice-convex windows, including empty erosions and low dimension. Zero/nonzero backgrounds, unequal tails and higher periods were allowed throughout. An added doubly periodic background is absorbed as in CN Remark 0.1; the bridge then keeps that star's original chosen $H_i$.

## 8. Deletion and reuse

| CN module | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Section 2.1 | Shortened positive isolating limit |
| Lemmas 2.0–2.4 | Remove spectral construction and special encoding; use the scalar bridge |
| Lemma 2.5 / Remark 2.6 | Rewrite using $\varphi,Z'$ and retain empty erosion |
| Section 3 | Remove sector adjacency and color-background gluing; use finite codimension and one cone |
| Lemma 4.1 | Move and reprove; not counted as deleted |
| Lemmas 4.2, 5.1 | Retain witness existence; rewrite both recursions |
| Lemma 5.2 through Theorem 7.3 | Retain and check with new roots, degrees, zonotope and witness |

The old modules construct full color spectra and a color-vector background; downstream only needs the three scalar interfaces. Corollary 24(a) adds a substantive logical input to Theorem A even though CN cites KS elsewhere. We claim no shortening after expanding KS's upstream proof. Original Appendix C certificates are not transferred to the new parameters.

## 9. Changed parameters and negative controls

For $p=5$, take $F_1(x,0)=1$ at $x\equiv0\pmod4$, $F_1(x,0)=2$ at $x\equiv2\pmod4$, zero elsewhere; take $F_2=3\mathbf1[x=1]$. Both components are not doubly periodic, have zero tails, and $H_1=4e_1,H_2=e_2$. Disjoint supports make every nonzero-color indicator periodic in its component direction; the zero-color indicator is the constant minus their sum. This is globally Case B.

With $(w(0),\ldots,w(4))=(0,-1,1,3,4)$,
$$
\eta(x,y)=a(x)\mathbf1[y=0]+3\mathbf1[x=1],\qquad a=(-1,0,1,0)\text{ of period }4.
$$
The minimal recurrence of $a$ is $t^2+1$: $a(x+2)=-a(x)$, while evaluation at $x=0,1$ excludes degree one. Grouping by transverse layers gives the component ideals $(T_1^2+1)$ and $(T_2-1)$. If an operator kills their sum, its horizontal output has finitely many rows, its vertical output finitely many columns. Cancellation would make the horizontally periodic output finite-support, hence zero; both outputs vanish. Therefore
$$
\operatorname{Ann}(\eta)=((T_1^2+1)(T_2-1)),\quad \mathcal H=R,\quad Z'=[0,2e_1]+[0,e_2].
$$
Here intersection equals product by coprime polynomial factors, not comaximal ideals. CN's color-1 row $(1,0,0,0)$ has all four fourth-root Fourier coefficients nonzero; hence its original $A=(T_1^4-1)(T_2-1)\ne\varphi$. For $d=(1,1)$, put $h(z)=\eta(z)\eta(z+d)$. Globally,
$$
\eta(z)\eta(z+d)=-3\mathbf1[z=(0,0)]+3\mathbf1[z=(1,-1)],\qquad (Dh)(0,0)=-3,
$$
Here $d=(1,1)-(0,0)$, and both $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ lie in $Z'$. These are analytic identities, not finite sampling.

Two negative controls: $c=(-1)^x$ is doubly periodic and killed by $(T_1-1)(T_2-1)$, but $T_1c=-c$, so individual invariance needs the cone proof. Also $c=\mathbf1[y=0]$ has ideal $(T_1-1)$ despite being killed by that product. Adding a zero vertical component violates S2; $\varphi\mid D$ alone does not ensure every direction occurs.

## 10. References and AI disclosure

We credit KS's ideal structure and CN's retained mechanisms. Priority is unverified; significance remains for reviewers. References: [CN](https://math.apexin.net/papers/convex-nivat.pdf), Sections 0–7; KS, *An Algebraic Geometric Approach to Nivat's Conjecture*, [arXiv:1605.05929v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.05929v1), Theorem 21 / Corollary 24(a). CN is *The Convex Nivat Conjecture: A Complexity Lower Bound for Star Configurations, and a Reduction from Low Convex Complexity to Star Configurations*, dated 12 September 2026. 6.title: Theorem B（定理 8.18）的 Lean 形式化验证：完整证明依赖、题意对应与公理审计
6.excerpt_md: **对应位置：** 论文 03，Theorem B / 定理 8.18。 **贡献类别：** 关键验证（形式化验证）。
6.body_md:
**对应位置：** 论文 03，Theorem B / 定理 8.18。  
**贡献类别：** 关键验证（形式化验证）。

### 1. 验证结果

已完成凸 Nivat 结论及其所需证明依赖的 Lean 形式化，并在 GitHub Actions 的全新 Linux 环境中通过完整编译、题意对应检查和公理审计。

所验证的命题为：

设 $A$ 为有限字母表，$\xi:\mathbb Z^2\to A$ 为配置，$S\subseteq\mathbb Z^2$ 为非空有限集，满足

$$
S=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}(S)\cap\mathbb Z^2.
$$

记实际出现的平移图案数为

$$
P_\xi(S)=
\left|\left\{(s\mapsto\xi(u+s))\in A^S:
u\in\mathbb Z^2\right\}\right|.
$$

若 $P_\xi(S)\leq |S|$，则存在非零整数向量 $h$，使得

$$
\forall u\in\mathbb Z^2,\qquad \xi(u+h)=\xi(u).
$$

### 2. 形式化实现与题意对应

最终定理为：

`NivatTrial.TheoremB.periodic_of_low_convex_complexity`

其假设直接对应有限字母表、非空有限格点凸窗口和实际图案复杂度上界。所需的整数分解与区域构造均已在项目内证明，最终定理没有额外的外部结果参数。

为核对题意，项目设置了两个文件：

- `Statements.lean` 仅导入 Mathlib，直接定义格点凸性、实际图案集合和非零全局周期，陈述 `ConvexNivatStatement.ConvexNivat`。
- `Audit.lean` 证明这些定义与项目定义的对应关系，并从最终定理推出 `ReleaseAudit.convex_nivat : ConvexNivatStatement.ConvexNivat`。

题意对应关系与最终推导均经过 Lean 检查。

### 3. 公开源码与核验记录

- [源码仓库及构建说明](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/convex-nivat-lean)
- [通过核验的固定提交](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/convex-nivat-lean/tree/5674e77aabc7235b733b7111ad71c18b3fe5c74b)
- [CI 运行记录](https://github.com/Rogerhu12/convex-nivat-lean/actions/runs/36665504290)

该次 CI 于 2026 年 9 月 30 日成功完成，结果如下：

| 检查项 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 完整编译 | 219 个数学模块通过 |
| 数学源码规模 | 27,091 行非空、非注释代码，不含 Mathlib |
| 题意对应与最终推导 | 通过 |
| 公理审计 | 覆盖 3,791 个声明，其中 3,182 个 theorem 声明 |
| 传递公理依赖 | 仅 `propext`、`Classical.choice`、`Quot.sound` |
| 源码一致性与检查器测试 | 通过；5 项测试全部成功 |

证明源码未使用 `sorry`、`admit` 或额外声明的公理。

环境固定为 Lean 4.33.0，Mathlib 提交为：

`db584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d`

取得仓库并切换到上述核验提交后，可按 README 安装环境并运行：

```sh
lake exe cache get
python3 check.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
lake build
lake env lean Audit.lean
```

### 4. 证明路线与贡献说明

验证范围为 Theorem B 的最终结论及实际采用的完整证明链。各模块与原文的对应关系、实现中的路线调整，记录在 `PROOF_MAP.md` 及相关审查文档中。

其中，Colle Case 1 采用以下实现：固定同一个非周期配置，合并具有共同长边种子的有限一致窗口，取有向并形成区域，再通过反射复用 Case 2 的第二边界论证。这是对原 Claim 4.7 角扇区扩张路线的替代实现。

候选论证及所引用数学结果归其原作者；本项贡献是 Lean 形式化实现、证明路线调整和可复现核验材料。形式化实现与内部复核使用 Codex AI 代理完成，包括 GPT-6-sol / xhigh 子代理。

4.title: Verification of Theorem A for Star Configurations in the Convex Nivat Paper
4.excerpt_md: This note verifies the full proof chain of Theorem A, for star configurations, in Sections 0–7 of Apex Intelligence, *The Convex Nivat Conje…
4.body_md:
This note verifies the full proof chain of Theorem A, for star configurations, in Sections 0–7 of Apex Intelligence, *The Convex Nivat Conjecture: A Complexity Lower Bound for Star Configurations, and a Reduction from Low Convex Complexity to Star Configurations*. The conclusion is $P_\theta(S)\geq |S|+1$ for every nonempty finite lattice-convex window $S$. The reduction from general low-complexity configurations in Section 8 and Appendix D is outside this verification. We also identify an explanatory error in Appendix C that does not affect this proof chain.

Source: [official PDF](https://math.apexin.net/papers/convex-nivat.pdf), published 2026-09-12, 891,962 bytes, SHA-256 `7fd67831155f4226c010fd6af32de558b76643771e6be12dea4eebafa21745a8`. References below use printed pages. Theorem A: p.2; Theorem T: p.4; Theorem 7.3: p.18. Manuscript **v1.2**; archive [v1.1](https://github.com/iamwangxi/apex-p03-nivat-theorem-a-validation/tree/v1.1). Expanded proofs: `proof/upstream-proof.md` and `proof/expanded-proof.md`.

## 1. Hypotheses, common periods and Case A

Fix a prime $p$. A star configuration is a sum $\theta=\sum_{i=1}^m F_i:\mathbb Z^2\to\mathbb F_p$, with $m\geq2$, pairwise nonparallel primitive integer directions $v_i$, and periods $k_i v_i$ of $F_i$, $k_i\geq1$. Each $F_i$ is not doubly periodic. There are doubly periodic tails $L_i,R_i$ and integers $\ell_i\leq r_i+1$ such that $F_i=L_i$ where $\pi_i<\ell_i$ and $F_i=R_i$ where $\pi_i>r_i$, with $\pi_i(z)=\det(v_i,z)$. Empty transition strips and unequal tails are allowed. Colors are added in $\mathbb F_p$; indicators, integer encodings, Laurent operators and dimensions below are in characteristic zero.

The intersection $\Gamma$ of the period lattices of all tails has finite index. Choose $\kappa_i\in k_i\mathbb Z_{>0}$ with $H_i=\kappa_i v_i\in\Gamma$. Each $H_i$ preserves its own component and every tail. Write

$$
T^u f(z)=f(z+u),\qquad D=\prod_i(T^{H_i}-1),\qquad I_a=\mathbf1[\theta=a].
$$

The operator $D$ is a nonzero Laurent polynomial. In its expansion retain formal subsets $C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ with $H_C=\sum_{i\in C}H_i$, even when different subsets give the same vector.

For a local function $h(z)=\varphi(\theta|_{z+W})$ with nonempty finite $W$, put $M=W+\{H_C\}_C$, $a_i=\max_{s\in M}|\pi_i(s)|$ and $\Sigma_i=\{z:\ell_i-a_i\leq\pi_i(z)\leq r_i+a_i\}$. Outside $\Sigma_i$ the whole stencil lies in one side’s tail, including when the transition strip is empty. Outside all pairwise strip intersections, at most one direction, say $j$, is active. The local configuration is its component plus fixed tails, all preserved by $H_j$. Pair subsets not containing $j$ with their union with $\{j\}$; the corresponding windows agree and their terms cancel. Thus $\operatorname{supp}(Dh)$ lies in finitely many intersections of nonparallel strips, a finite set of lattice points. An empty $W$ gives a constant and $Dh=0$. This proves Lemma 1.1 (pp.5–6) globally.

If $J$ has nonzero finite support, then $\widehat J(X)=\sum_z J(z)X^{-z}$ is a nonzero Laurent polynomial, and

$$
\widehat{f(T)J}(X)=f(X)\widehat J(X)\ne0\qquad(f\ne0).
$$

This proves Lemma 1.2 (p.6). In Case A, some $DI_a\ne0$. If $P_\theta(S)\leq|S|$ for a nonempty finite $S$, the $|S|+1$ rational functions $1,\mathbf1[\gamma(s)=a]$ on the complete translated pattern set are dependent. They yield a nonzero $f(T)=\sum_{s\in S}c_sT^s$ with $f(T)I_a$ constant. Applying $D$ contradicts Lemma 1.2. Proposition 1.3 (p.6) closes Case A for every nonempty finite window.

Henceforth Case B means $DI_a=0$ for every color. Consequently $Dg(\theta)=0$ for every single-site color function $g$, including both the encoding and its square used below.

## 2. One encoding preserves every exceptional frequency

For each $i$ and sign $\sigma$, the translates along $\sigma nH_i$ stabilize on every finite set to $\Xi_i^\sigma=F_i+B_i^\sigma$. Here $B_i^\sigma$ sums the right tail of component $j\ne i$ when $\sigma\pi_j(v_i)>0$, and its left tail otherwise. Common tail periods fix phases throughout the limit. Thus $\Xi_i^\sigma$ is in the orbit closure $X_\theta$. Choose a lattice basis $(v_i,u_i)$ of determinant one and $N\mathbb Z^2\subseteq\Gamma$. Translating this limit along $\pm nNu_i$ also gives the pure tails $G_i^{\sigma,\epsilon}=\epsilon_i+B_i^\sigma$, for $\epsilon=L,R$, in $X_\theta$.

The color differences

$$
\delta_{i,\sigma,\epsilon,a}=\mathbf1[\Xi_i^\sigma=a]-\mathbf1[G_i^{\sigma,\epsilon}=a]
$$

are $H_i$-periodic and vanish on the corresponding entire half-plane. For $\lambda^{\kappa_i}=1$ use the cyclic Fourier projections

$$
P_\lambda=\frac1{\kappa_i}\sum_{k=0}^{\kappa_i-1}\lambda^{-k}T^{kv_i}.
$$

Let $\Lambda_i$ contain the frequencies appearing nontrivially in some such difference. If it were empty, all color differences would vanish, forcing $F_i$ to equal a doubly periodic tail. Set

$$
d_i=|\Lambda_i|\geq1,\quad A_i(t)=\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda_i}(t-\lambda),\quad
A(T)=\prod_i A_i(T^{v_i}),\quad Z=\sum_i[0,d_iv_i].
$$

Each $A_i$ is monic, divides $t^{\kappa_i}-1$, and has nonzero constant term. It kills every corresponding color difference. Newton polygons multiply by Minkowski addition, so $\operatorname{Newt}(A)=Z$, a two-dimensional lattice zonotope.

For each pair $(i,\lambda)$ choose one nonzero Fourier coefficient vector across colors, at a fixed normal coordinate and fixed choices of tails. Requiring its weighted sum to be nonzero excludes a proper rational linear subspace of $\mathbb Q^p$. Also exclude the hyperplanes where two color weights coincide. Finitely many proper subspaces cannot cover $\mathbb Q^p$. Choose a single rational weight vector outside all of them, then clear denominators. The resulting integer injection $w:\mathbb F_p\to\mathbb Z$ preserves all the $\Lambda_i$ simultaneously. Injectivity alone would not prove this. Fix $\eta=w(\theta)$; Case B gives $D\eta=D(\eta^2)=0$.

For Lemma 2.3 (p.9), let a one-sided-vanishing $H_i$-periodic difference have nonzero $\lambda$ projection and be killed by $f(T)$. In coordinates $X=T^{v_i},Y=T^{u_i}$, the projected sequence satisfies $f(\lambda,Y)c=0$, where $c\ne0$ and vanishes on one end of the integer line. If it vanishes on the right, use its largest nonzero index and the smallest exponent of a purported nonzero $f(\lambda,Y)$; exactly one term survives. The left-vanishing case uses the opposite extrema. Hence $f(\lambda,Y)=0$ and $X-\lambda$ divides $f$.

If $f(T)\eta=c$ is constant, it holds on the entire orbit closure: each anchor imposes a closed condition depending on finitely many coordinates. Apply it separately to $\Xi_i^\sigma$ and $G_i^{\sigma,\epsilon}$ before subtracting. The preserved frequencies and Lemma 2.3 give $T^{v_i}-\lambda\mid f$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda_i$. Each factor is prime in the complex Laurent ring, since a primitive $v_i$ extends to a lattice basis and the quotient by $X-\lambda$ is a Laurent domain. Distinct roots and nonparallel directions give nonassociated factors. Their product therefore divides $f$: this proves Lemma 2.4 (pp.9–10).

## 3. The affine budget, including degenerate windows

For finite nonempty $S$ let $\mathcal L_S$ be all translated patterns, pulled back to $S$, and put

$$
U_S=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{1,\gamma\mapsto w(\gamma(s)):s\in S\},\qquad
R_Z(S)=\{r\in\mathbb Z^2:r+Z\subseteq\operatorname{Conv}(S)\}.
$$

The rational relation space among these functions is defined by rows $(-1,(\eta(u+s))_{s\in S})$ for all integer anchors $u$. Its row space has a basis selected from at most $|S|+1$ actual rational rows. Thus the infinite system is equivalent to one finite rational system, whose rank is unchanged over $\mathbb C$.

For a nonzero complex relation $f(T)\eta=c_0$, Lemma 2.4 gives $f=Ag$. The nonzero $f$ uniquely determines $c_0$. Newton multiplication gives

$$
Z+\operatorname{Newt}(g)=\operatorname{Newt}(f)\subseteq\operatorname{Conv}(S),
$$

so $\operatorname{supp}(g)\subseteq R_Z(S)$. Division by $A$ is an injective linear map from the relation space into the coefficient space supported there. Since $0\in Z$, this set is finite. Lemma 2.5 (p.10) follows:

$$
\dim_{\mathbb Q}U_S\geq |S|+1-|R_Z(S)|.
$$

If $R_Z(S)$ is empty, this already proves the theorem. In particular, point and segment windows have this property because $Z$ has interior. Two-dimensional windows with empty $R_Z(S)$ are covered too.

## 4. A global periodic background, then a genuine witness

The $m$ direction lines have $2m$ actual open sectors. Across a boundary ray $\sigma v_i$, adjacent sector tails are precisely $G_i^{\sigma,L}$ and $G_i^{\sigma,R}$. Their color-indicator difference is killed by $A_i$, hence by $A$. Connectivity of the cyclic list of sectors shows that their images under $A$ are one common doubly periodic vector field $b$, preserved by every $H_i$ (Lemma 3.1, p.11). No statement about all formal tail combinations is needed.

Here is an explicit finite exceptional region for Lemma 3.2 (p.12). Put $M=\operatorname{supp}(A)$, choose integers $c_i\geq1+\max(|\ell_i|,|r_i|)$, and let

$$
\rho_i=c_i+\max_{s\in M}|\pi_i(s)|,\qquad \Sigma_i=\{z:|\pi_i(z)|\leq\rho_i\}.
$$

With no active strip, the entire stencil lies in an actual sector-tail configuration. With at least two active strips the anchor belongs to their bounded intersection. With only direction $i$ active write $z=tv_i+qu_i$, $|q|\leq\rho_i$, and set

$$
B_i=\frac{\rho_i\max_{j\ne i}|\pi_j(u_i)|+\max_{j\ne i}\rho_j}
{\min_{j\ne i}|\pi_j(v_i)|}.
$$

The denominator is positive. If $|t|>B_i$, every other component on $z+M$ has the tail prescribed by $\operatorname{sign}(t\pi_j(v_i))$. The whole stencil agrees with $\Xi_i^{\operatorname{sign}(t)}$, whose image under $A$ equals the appropriate adjacent-sector image. Thus $Ae_\theta-b$ is supported in the finite set consisting of the pairwise strip intersections and the lattice boxes $|q|\leq\rho_i,|t|\leq B_i$ in these bases. Here $e_\theta=(I_a)_a$.

Case B and periodicity give $D(Ae_\theta-b)=0$. Lemma 1.2 forces this finite remainder to vanish identically. Proposition 3.3 (p.12) holds globally:

$$
Ae_\theta=b,\qquad A\eta=b_\eta=\sum_a w(a)b_a.
$$

Every $H_i$ preserves the possibly nonzero $b_\eta$.

For Lemma 4.1 (p.13) set $Q_i=\prod_{j\ne i}(T^{H_j}-1)$ and $f_i=Q_i\eta$. Case B makes $f_i$ $H_i$-periodic. Passing along $nH_i$ to the isolation limit, then subtracting either pure tail, gives globally

$$
f_i=Q_i\bigl(w(\Xi_i^+)-w(G_i^{+,R})\bigr)
=Q_i\bigl(w(\Xi_i^+)-w(G_i^{+,L})\bigr).
$$

The two one-sided vanishings bound its support in a strip parallel to $v_i$. The right-tail difference is nonzero by injectivity and non-double-periodicity, with a largest nonzero normal coordinate. In the formal expansion of $Q_i$, the subset $\{j\ne i:\pi_i(H_j)<0\}$ uniquely minimizes the normal displacement, since every $\pi_i(H_j)\ne0$. Evaluating at the largest nonzero row shifted by this minimum leaves exactly one nonzero term. Thus $f_i\ne0$ even when other subset sums collide.

Choose $i\ne j$ and points $x_i,x_j$ where these strip fields are nonzero. With $d_0=x_j-x_i$, the product $C(z)=f_i(z)f_j(z+d_0)$ is nonzero and finitely supported. Hence $DC\ne0$. Expanding both $Q$ operators expresses $DC$ as a finite signed sum of translates of

$$
J(d,z)=D_z[\eta(z)\eta(z+d)].
$$

At least one $J(d,\cdot)$ is nonzero. Each fixed $d$ has finite support by Lemma 1.1, and $J(0,\cdot)=D(\eta^2)=0$. This proves Lemma 4.2 (pp.13–14).

## 5. Quotient algebra and localization of that witness

Write $A(T)=\sum_s A_sT^s$. The global background identity yields Lemma 5.1 (p.14):

$$
\sum_s A_sJ(d+s,z)=0,\qquad \sum_s A_sJ(d-s,z+s)=0.
$$

These are $D_z[\eta(z)b_\eta(z+d)]$ and $D_z[b_\eta(z)\eta(z+d)]$. In the formal subset expansion the background is unchanged and factors out; $D\eta=0$ then applies. No differential Leibniz rule is used.

Set $K=\mathbb C(X_1,X_2)$, $R=K[Y_1^{\pm1},Y_2^{\pm1}]$, $a_i=A_i(Y^{v_i})$, $c_i=A_i(X^{v_i}Y^{-v_i})$, $a=\prod_i a_i$, $c=\prod_i c_i$. The reused constructive proof of Lemma 5.2 (pp.15–16) establishes

$$
R/(a,c)\simeq\prod_{i\ne j}R/(a_i,c_j),\qquad
\dim_K R/(a,c)=\sum_{i\ne j}|\det(v_i,v_j)|d_i d_j,
$$

and spanning by $Y^e$ with $e\in(Z-Z)\cap\mathbb Z^2$.

First, $(a_i,c_i)=R$ follows by univariate Euclid: a common root would make the transcendental $X^{v_i}$ a product of constant roots. For $i\ne k$, choose a positive $N$ with $Nv_j=\alpha\kappa_iv_i+\beta\kappa_kv_k$ for integers $\alpha,\beta$. The identities $(t-1)S_n(t)=t^n-1$, with finite Laurent sums also for negative $n$, express $Y^{Nv_j}-1$ in $(a_i,a_k)$. Euclid applied to $t^N-1$ and $t^{d_j}A_j(X^{v_j}/t)$ then gives $(a_i,a_k,c_j)=R$. The involution $Y^u\mapsto X^uY^{-u}$ yields $(a_i,c_j,c_\ell)=R$ for $j\ne\ell$. Multiplying the witnesses over $j$ gives $(a_i,a_k,c)=R$, the needed merging step for CRT in $R/(c)$. CRT again in each $R/(a_i)$, where $c_i$ is a unit, gives the displayed product.

For component $(i,j)$, representatives $r$ in the half-open parallelogram $\{\rho v_i-\tau v_j:0\leq\rho,\tau<1\}$ split the Laurent ring into lattice cosets. Monic division in $Y^{v_i}$ and $Y^{-v_j}$ gives a basis with exponents

$$
r+\alpha v_i-\beta v_j,\qquad 0\leq\alpha<d_i,\quad 0\leq\beta<d_j.
$$

Nonzero constant terms make both variables invertible; monic division remains valid over the first quotient even if it has zero divisors. There are $|\det(v_i,v_j)|d_i d_j$ basis vectors. Put $E_{ij}=\prod_{k\ne i}a_k\prod_{\ell\ne j}c_\ell$. It vanishes in other components and is a unit in its own. Expand the inverse times any desired component in the local basis, then multiply by $E_{ij}$. The resulting spanning vectors have support in

$$
\sum_{k\ne i}[0,d_kv_k]+\sum_{\ell\ne j}[0,-d_\ell v_\ell]
 +[0,d_iv_i]+[0,-d_jv_j]=Z-Z.
$$

No support bound on the inverse is needed.

Define a $K$-linear functional by $L(Y^d)=\widehat J(d;X)=\sum_zJ(d,z)X^{-z}$. Separate finite support for each $d$ suffices. The first recurrence kills all $Y^da$; changing variables $z'=z+s$ in the second contributes $X^{+s}$ and kills all $Y^dc$. Linearity kills the whole ideal $(a,c)$. If all $J(d,\cdot)$ with $d\in Z-Z$ vanished, the spanning theorem would force $L=0$, contrary to the genuine witness. Proposition 5.3 (pp.16–17) therefore gives a fixed nonzero $d\in(Z-Z)\cap\mathbb Z^2$ with $J(d,\cdot)\ne0$.

## 6. Two lattice sites and completion of Theorem A

For Lemma 6.1 (p.17), put $c_0=\sum_i d_iv_i$. Central symmetry gives $Z-Z=2Z-c_0$. For $x=d+c_0\in2Z\cap\mathbb Z^2$, take a lattice triangle in $Z$ containing $x/2$. Refine at nonvertex lattice points, keeping a nondegenerate closed subtriangle containing $x/2$, until it is unimodular. Positive integer normalized area strictly decreases; the companion proof gives the lattice-point construction and treats boundary points. In the final unimodular triangle, twice the two barycentric coordinates are nonnegative integers of sum at most two. The six possibilities express $x$ as the sum of two vertices. Reflection about $c_0/2$ gives lattice points $q,q+d\in Z$.

Apply this construction to the nonzero witness already fixed in Proposition 5.3. Fix $q$ next, before choosing a window: the quantifier order is $\exists d\,\exists q\,\forall S$. For lattice-convex $S$ and $r\in R_Z(S)$ the sites $r+q,r+q+d$ are in $S$. Define

$$
\Phi_r(\gamma)=w(\gamma(r+q))w(\gamma(r+q+d)).
$$

If a nontrivial rational combination of these functions belonged to $U_S$, substitution of every translated pattern and application of $D$ would give

$$
\left(\sum_r c_rT^{r+q}\right)J(d,\cdot)=0.
$$

The operator is nonzero because its exponents are distinct. The witness is nonzero with finite support, contradicting Lemma 1.2. Thus Lemma 7.2 (p.18) gives independence modulo $U_S$, and

$$
P_\theta(S)\geq\dim U_S+|R_Z(S)|\geq|S|+1.
$$

Together with Case A and the empty-$R_Z(S)$ branch, this completes the theorem under its original star-configuration assumptions. We claim no stronger bound or additional class of windows here.

## 7. Appendix C: one explanatory error, no break in the chain

Remark 3.1′ (p.11) and Appendix C.3 (p.32) use a three-direction example to argue against equality after applying the full product $A$ to arbitrary tail combinations. Its directions are $(1,0),(0,-1),(1,-1)$; all tails depend only on the horizontal coordinate, and the vertical component and its isolation backgrounds do also. Thus its nonempty exceptional spectrum is $\Lambda_2=\{1\}$, giving the factor $A_2=T^{(0,-1)}-1$. This factor kills the color indicators of every one of the eight tail combinations, so the full $A$ kills them all. The displayed mixed difference has horizontal period-six values $(-1,0,1,0,1,0)$; applying $A_1=T^{(2,0)}-1$ gives $(2,0,0,0,-2,0)$. That valid single-factor calculation does not establish the claimed full-product counterexample. Whether the general arbitrary-tail extension holds under Case B remains unproved here. The main proof uses only actual sectors, so this error has no effect on Theorem A and is not a separate challenge submission. The companion audit also checks Observation C.1 (pp.31–32) under its stated $m=2,L_i=R_i$ assumptions; Appendix C's random experiments are not independently certified.

## 8. Reused evidence, new verification and AI disclosure

The new contribution is upstream certification and full-chain integration, closing the earlier module’s conditional premises. The constructive algebraic module, lattice construction, two global examples and twelve frozen inputs are reused supporting evidence, not new coverage or a second module submission.

The two global examples have respectively 347 and 401 complete translated patterns, witness supports of 12 and 32 points, and rational matrix ranks $46\to55$ established by integer minors and kernel vectors. The second has the genuine nonzero background $A\eta=4$. The archive includes global coverage proofs and exact certificates. The twelve algebraic inputs cover two to four directions, reversed orientations, negative determinants, nonprimitive directions, indices up to eleven and cyclotomic products. They do not assert twelve star configurations or relax the theorem’s hypotheses.

The saved rational certificates contain 163 basic unit identities, 46 local inverse identities and 128 local basis/spanning vectors for those twelve inputs. The standard-library checker reconstructs targets from the frozen inputs and checks exact integer/Fraction identities, component completeness and support. It imports no generator. Symbolic generation uses pinned SymPy only for optional regeneration. The archive's checking command is:


The full suite, including the symbolic gate and both examples, has fifteen checks and 368 prescribed negative controls; packaging records document the rerun. 9.body_md:
投稿人：[投稿人]  
联系邮箱：[redacted-email]  
贡献类别：关键验证（verification）  
对应论文：Apex Intelligence, The Convex Nivat Conjecture: A Complexity Lower Bound for Star Configurations, and a Reduction from Low Convex Complexity to Star Configurations，活动页面提供的 2026 年 9 月 12 日版本。  
具体位置：第 5.2 节，引理 5.2，第 15–16 页；直接用途为第 5.3 节命题 5.3，第 16–17 页。  
文件 SHA256：7fd67831155f4226c010fd6af32de558b76643771e6be12dea4eebafa21745a8。

## 摘要

本投稿核验引理 5.2 中把商代数限制到有限 Newton 区域的关键步骤。完整论证明确了三点：所用理想在商环中确实互素，而不只是多项式没有公因子；非幺模方向需要完整的格陪集代表；投影乘子在目标因子上可逆已足够，不需要其逆也有小支撑。由此给出支撑位于 Z−Z 的显式基，并得到精确维数公式。附带七个精确有理数计算特例及可复现代码，保存 Gröbner 基、标准单项式、基的正规形矩阵与非零行列式。

这是对原文核心代数模块的独立核验和展开。维数公式是原证明机制的直接强化，不主张首次发现，不申报“突破贡献”。没有发现此模块的实质错误，也不据此声称整篇凸形 Nivat 猜想证明已经认证。本文不包含 Lean 形式化证明。

AI 辅助说明：推导整理、代码编写和多轮自动化交叉检查使用了 AI 辅助。本文提供可逐步审阅的数学证明与可执行检查，不将 AI 的判断或有限测试当作普遍命题的证明；也不声称投稿人本人已逐行阅读或手工核验全部推导与代码。本文尚未获得活动方专家评审结论。

## 主结果依赖定位与本投稿范围

已对照原文摘要、引言和第5至8节核对以下主要依赖路线。Theorem A 即 Theorem 7.3：Lemma 2.5 给出仿射维数下界，Lemma 7.2 给出补足缺额的二次可观测量独立性；后者使用 Proposition 5.3 的非零见证、Lemma 6.1 和 Corollary 6.2 的格点差表示，并用 Lemma 1.2 与式(1.1)完成消去。Proposition 5.3 在此前递推关系和非零性成立的条件下，使用 Lemma 5.2 将见证位移限制到 Z-Z。本投稿一般证明独立覆盖的正是这个商代数步骤。

Theorem B 即 Theorem 8.18：原文的主要路线为 Theorem 8.4（Kari-Szabados）-> Lemma 8.5 -> Theorems 8.6及8.7（Colle）-> Proposition 8.9 -> Theorem 8.12（使用附录D的Theorem D.1）-> Lemma 8.17 -> Theorem 7.3。此处给出依赖定位，不把局部核验扩张为对这条完整路线或全部引用定理的认证。

提交前核查说明：2026-10-01在独立目录重新执行四个公开检查脚本，均通过。七个精确商代数特例、独立证书和格点支撑核查与一般证明分别陈述；有限测试不替代一般证明。未完成Lean形式化，也未获得投稿人本人逐行人工复核或领域专家审定。

## 1. Exact statement and notation

Let m≥2. Let $v_1$,…,$v_m$ be nonzero, pairwise nonparallel vectors in Z². Let $A_i$(t)∈C[t] have degree $d_i$≥1 and nonzero constant term. Set

$$
K=\mathbb{C}(X_1,X_2),\qquad R=K[Y_1^{\pm1},Y_2^{\pm1}]
$$

$$
a_i=A_i(Y^{v_i}),\qquad c_i=A_i(X^{v_i}Y^{-v_i})
$$

$$
a=\prod_i a_i,\qquad c=\prod_i c_i,\qquad Z=\sum_i[0,d_i v_i]
$$

The X coordinates are algebraically independent. For e=($e_1$,$e_2$), $Y^e$ means $Y_1^{e_1}Y_2^{e_2}$, and $X^e$ is defined similarly. Support means the finite set of exponent vectors with nonzero coefficients, and sums of segments are Minkowski sums.

For i≠j, let $P_{ij}$=[0,$d_i$ $v_i$]+[0,−$d_j$ $v_j$]. Choose the lattice points r in the half-open parallelogram

$$
\Pi_{ij}=\{s v_i-t v_j:0\leq s<1,\ 0\leq t<1\}
$$

There are $\nu_{ij}$=|det($v_i$,$v_j$)| such points. Define

$$
E_{ij}=\left(\prod_{k\ne i}a_k\right)\left(\prod_{l\ne j}c_l\right)
$$

Claim. The images in R/(a,c) of the following finite collection form a K-basis:

$$
E_{ij}Y^{r+\alpha v_i-\beta v_j}
$$

$$
i\ne j,\quad r\in\Pi_{ij}\cap\mathbb{Z}^2,\quad 0\leq\alpha<d_i,\quad0\leq\beta<d_j
$$

$$
\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{Z}
$$

Every representative in this collection has support in (Z−Z)∩Z². Consequently

$$
\dim_K R/(a,c)=\sum_{i\ne j}d_i d_j|\det(v_i,v_j)|
$$

and the images of the monomials $Y^e$, e∈(Z−Z)∩Z², span the quotient, as required by Lemma 5.2.

The original lemma has stronger hypotheses: its directions are primitive and its $A_i$ arise from exceptional roots of unity. The proof here does not require primitivity, squarefreeness or roots of unity. This observation is used to stress-test the algebra, not as a separate prize claim.

## 2. Comaximal ideals and the exact CRT decomposition

Work temporarily over an algebraic closure $\overline K$ and evaluate on the torus $(\overline K^{\times})^2$. Every root of an $A_i$ is a nonzero complex number.

First, $a_i$=$c_i$=0 would imply $Y^{v_i}$=λ and $X^{v_i}Y^{-v_i}$=μ for λ,μ∈$\mathbb{C}^{\times}$. Multiplication gives $X^{v_i}$=λμ, impossible because $v_i$≠0 and the X coordinates are independent.

Second, if $a_i$=$a_k$=0 with i≠k, the nonzero determinant gives $Y_1^\Delta$ and $Y_2^\Delta$ as products of integer powers of two complex roots, for Δ=det($v_i$,$v_k$). Thus both Y coordinates are algebraic over C and hence belong to $\mathbb{C}^{\times}$, since C is algebraically closed. Any $c_j$=0 would then force $X^{v_j}$ to be a complex constant, again impossible.

Third, if $c_j$=$c_l$=0 with j≠l, apply the preceding determinant argument to W=X/Y. Both W coordinates lie in $\mathbb{C}^{\times}$, so $Y_1$=αX_1 and $Y_2$=βX_2 for nonzero complex α,β. No $a_i$ can then vanish.

The Laurent Nullstellensatz and faithful flatness of extension from K to $\overline K$ give the unit ideals

$$
(a_i,c_i)=R
$$

$$
(a_i,a_k,c)=R\ (i\ne k),\qquad (a_i,c_j,c_l)=R\ (j\ne l)
$$

For clarity, the second assertion holds because c=0 implies some $c_j$=0. These are actual unit-ideal statements, not deductions from pairwise polynomial gcds.

In R/(c), the principal ideals generated by the $a_i$ are pairwise comaximal. For a finite pairwise-comaximal family their product equals their intersection, so the Chinese remainder theorem gives

$$
R/(a,c)\simeq\prod_i R/(a_i,c)
$$

In R/($a_i$), $c_i$ is a unit and the other $c_j$ generate pairwise-comaximal ideals. A second CRT therefore gives the natural projection isomorphism

$$
R/(a,c)\simeq\prod_{i\ne j} R/(a_i,c_j)\qquad (1)
$$

This argument does not assume that any ideal is radical. Repeated roots are allowed throughout.

## 3. Basis of an individual factor

Fix i≠j and write u=$Y^{v_i}$, w=$Y^{-v_j}$. The determinant is nonzero, so u,w are algebraically independent Laurent monomials. Put B=K[$u^{\pm1}$,$w^{\pm1}$] and L=Z $v_i$+Z(−$v_j$). Its index is $\nu_{ij}$.

Decomposing exponents into lattice cosets gives a free B-module decomposition

$$
R=\bigoplus_{r\in\Pi_{ij}\cap\mathbb{Z}^2}Y^r B
$$

The two generators $a_i$=$A_i$(u) and $c_j$=$A_j$($X^{v_j}$w) lie in B. Quotienting this free decomposition therefore gives

$$
R/(a_i,c_j)=\bigoplus_rY^r\left[B/(A_i(u),A_j(X^{v_j}w))\right]\qquad (2)
$$

The bracketed algebra is the tensor product over K of the two one-variable quotients. A degree-d polynomial with nonzero constant and leading coefficients makes its variable invertible modulo that polynomial. Thus localization loses no dimension, and the usual classes 1,u,…,$u^{d_i-1}$ and 1,w,…,$w^{d_j-1}$ are bases of their respective quotients. Their tensor products are a basis of the bracketed algebra.

It follows that the classes of $Y^{r+\alpha v_i-\beta v_j}$, with the indices stated in section 1, form a basis of the (i,j) factor, of dimension $\nu_{ij}$ $d_i$ $d_j$. The exponents belong to $P_{ij}$ because the two coefficients contributed by r lie in [0,1). This is precisely where the determinant-index representatives are needed; primitive directions alone would not make their determinant equal to ±1.

## 4. A global basis without small-support inverses

Under (1), $E_{ij}$ vanishes on any factor (i′,j′)≠(i,j). If i′≠i, it contains the vanishing factor $a_{i'}$; if i′=i but j′≠j, it contains $c_{j'}$.

On its own factor, every $a_k$ with k≠i is a unit: the ideal ($a_i$,$c_j$,$a_k$) has no torus zero by section 2. Every $c_l$ with l≠j is likewise a unit. Therefore $E_{ij}$ is a unit in R/($a_i$,$c_j$).

Multiplication by this unit is a K-linear automorphism of that factor. Multiplying its basis from section 3 by $E_{ij}$ gives a basis of the corresponding single-coordinate summand in the finite product (1). Their union is a basis of R/(a,c). Equivalently, project any proposed linear relation onto one factor at a time and cancel its unit $E_{ij}$; all coefficients vanish.

For the support bound,

$$
\mathrm{supp}(E_{ij})\subseteq\sum_{k\ne i}[0,d_kv_k]+\sum_{l\ne j}[0,-d_lv_l]
$$

Adding any exponent in $P_{ij}$ gives a subset of

$$
\sum_k[0,d_kv_k]+\sum_l[0,-d_lv_l]=Z-Z
$$

Thus every proposed basis representative has the required support. This proof uses no support bound for $E_{ij}^{-1}$. Nor does it assert that $E_{ij}$ is an idempotent: invertibility on its target factor is sufficient.

## 5. Why this verifies a consequential step of Proposition 5.3

A nonzero K-linear functional on R/(a,c) cannot vanish on every monomial $Y^e$ with e∈(Z−Z)∩Z², because those classes span the quotient. If it also vanishes on 1, at least one such nonvanishing monomial has e≠0.

The paper applies this fact to the Laurent-transformed two-point observable after establishing that it annihilates the two recurrence relations and is nonzero. Conditional on those earlier identities, Lemma 5.2 restricts its witness displacement to the finite zonotope difference. That restriction is needed for the later convex-window argument. This submission verifies the quotient-algebra implication; it does not silently claim independent certification of every preceding dynamical identity.

## 6. An elementary worked example

Take $v_1$=(1,0), $v_2$=(0,1), and $A_1$(t)=$A_2$(t)=t−1. The two CRT factors are evaluation at ($Y_1$,$Y_2$)=(1,$X_2$) and ($X_1$,1). The two proposed basis elements are

$$
E_{12}=(Y_2-1)(X_1/Y_1-1)
$$

$$
E_{21}=(Y_1-1)(X_2/Y_2-1)
$$

Their evaluation matrix is diagonal with both diagonal entries ($X_1$−1)($X_2$−1), which is nonzero in K. Their supports lie in [−1,1]²=Z−Z. This directly verifies the dimension 2 and illustrates why no inverse multiplier is necessary.

## 7. Exact executable checks and their limitations

The accompanying Python program uses SymPy 1.14.0 over QQ, specializes X=(2,3), and models the Laurent ring with an extra variable I and relation I $Y_1$ $Y_2$−1=0. It computes a Gröbner basis, enumerates standard monomials, constructs the proposed basis, checks every support exponent, reduces all basis elements, and verifies an exactly nonzero determinant. It also checks the rank of all monomials in Z−Z.

Seven completed cases give matching quotient dimension, zonotope-monomial rank and constructed-basis rank:

1. v=(1,0),(0,1); A=t−1,t−1: 2.
2. v=(1,0),(1,3); A=t²−1,t²+1: 24.
3. v=(1,0),(0,1),(1,1); all A=t−1: 6.
4. v=(1,0),(1,2),(2,1); A=t−1,t²+t+1,t²−1: 36.
5. v=(1,−1),(1,1),(0,1); all A=t−1: 8.
6. v=(1,0),(0,1); A=(t−1)²,t−1: 4.
7. v=(2,0),(0,3); A=t−1,t−1: 12.

The last two cases explicitly test repeated roots and nonprimitive directions. All roots in these cases are roots of unity. The specialization avoids the forbidden coincidences: 2^a3^b is a root of unity only when a=b=0. This also prevents a zero of two a-factors from being a zero of a c-factor, and conversely. The finite specializations are cross-checks, not a proof for transcendental X or arbitrary inputs; sections 2–4 supply that proof.

The algebraic-independence and nonzero-constant-term hypotheses cannot simply be omitted. In the worked example, X=(1,1) makes the two relations associates, so the quotient is not zero-dimensional. With $A_1$(t)=t and $A_2$(t)=t−1, independent directions instead give the zero quotient, whereas the stated degree formula would give 2. These are checks on the necessity of scope, not counterexamples to the paper.

## 8. Review boundary and attribution

Additional bounded review of section 8 and Appendix D found no verified substantive gap in the checked half-plane, two-component-limit, compact-limit propagation and balanced-set mechanisms. A separate safe-direction enumeration passed 3,262 cases. These are background checks, not a second prize contribution in this submission. They do not turn this lemma verification into certification of the full conjecture.

The imported regional-extraction comparison used Colle’s public arXiv:1909.08195v4 author manuscript and the discussion in Colle–Garibaldi arXiv:2606.10193v1. It did not establish line-by-line identity with the subscription journal edition or independently reprove all imported symbolic-dynamics results.

Primary target: activity manuscript, https://math.apexin.net/ , Lemma 5.2 pp. 15–16 and Proposition 5.3 pp. 16–17, identified by the SHA256 above. The CRT decomposition, lattice-module method and multiplier construction are credited to that manuscript. The present contribution is their explicit verification, independence/dimension derivation and reproducible computational evidence, without a claim of research priority.


## 可直接复现的完整核心检验程序

环境：Python 3.10 以上、SymPy 1.14.0；不要使用 -O。将下列代码保存为 code/check_quotient_certificates.py，在其上一级目录运行 python code/check_quotient_certificates.py。程序会生成 results/certificates 下的七个精确证书。预期维数及两组秩依次为 2,24,6,36,8,4,12。有限计算仅作为上文证明的交叉检查。

```python
"""Exact rational specialization checks for convex-nivat Lemma 5.2.
Not a proof of the universal statement. X=(2,3) cannot be a torsion character
in any nonzero lattice direction, so the geometric disjointness used in the
paper remains valid for cyclotomic Ai under this specialization.
"""
import itertools, time, json
from pathlib import Path
from collections import deque
import sympy as s
Y1,Y2,I = s.symbols('Y1 Y2 I')
vars=(Y1,Y2,I)

def mul(p,q):
    r={}
    for (a,b),c in p.items():
        for (x,y),d in q.items(): r[a+x,b+y]=r.get((a+x,b+y),0)+c*d
    return {v:s.cancel(c) for v,c in r.items() if c}
def prod(polys):
    p={(0,0):s.Integer(1)}
    for q in polys:p=mul(p,q)
    return p

def eval_laurent(p):
    out=0
    for (a,b),c in p.items():
        k=max(0,-a,-b)
        out+=c*Y1**(a+k)*Y2**(b+k)*I**k
    return s.expand(out)
def clear(p):
    ax=min(a for a,b in p);by=min(b for a,b in p)
    return sum(c*Y1**(a-ax)*Y2**(b-by) for (a,b),c in p.items())
def cross(o,a,b):return (a[0]-o[0])*(b[1]-o[1])-(a[1]-o[1])*(b[0]-o[0])
def hull(points):
    pp=sorted(set(points));lo=[];hi=[]
    for p in pp:
        while len(lo)>1 and cross(lo[-2],lo[-1],p)<=0:lo.pop()
        lo.append(p)
    for p in pp[::-1]:
        while len(hi)>1 and cross(hi[-2],hi[-1],p)<=0:hi.pop()
        hi.append(p)
    return lo[:-1]+hi[:-1]
def inside(p,h):return all(cross(h[k],h[(k+1)%len(h)],p)>=0 for k in range(len(h)))
def det(v,w):return v[0]*w[1]-v[1]*w[0]
def reps(v,w):
    # Columns v and -w; exact half-open fundamental parallelogram.
    M=s.Matrix([[v[0],-w[0]],[v[1],-w[1]]]);Mi=M.inv()
    vertices=[(0,0),v,(-w[0],-w[1]),(v[0]-w[0],v[1]-w[1])]
    out=[]
    for x in range(min(t[0] for t in vertices),max(t[0] for t in vertices)+1):
        for y in range(min(t[1] for t in vertices),max(t[1] for t in vertices)+1):
            alpha,beta=Mi*s.Matrix([x,y])
            if 0<=alpha<1 and 0<=beta<1:out.append((x,y))
    assert len(out)==abs(det(v,w))
    return out

def check(name,vs,coeffs):
    start=time.time(); ds=[len(c)-1 for c in coeffs]
    aa=[{(k*v[0],k*v[1]):s.Integer(c) for k,c in enumerate(cs) if c} for v,cs in zip(vs,coeffs)]
    cc=[{(-a,-b):c*s.Integer(2)**a*s.Integer(3)**b for (a,b),c in p.items()} for p in aa]
    A=prod(aa);C=prod(cc)
    G=s.groebner([clear(A),clear(C),I*Y1*Y2-1],*vars,order='grevlex',domain=s.QQ)
    assert G.is_zero_dimensional
    lm=[tuple(g.LM(order=G.order).exponents) for g in G.polys]
    std=set();seen={(0,0,0)};todo=deque(seen)
    while todo:
        e=todo.popleft()
        if any(all(a>=b for a,b in zip(e,l)) for l in lm):continue
        std.add(e)
        for k in range(3):
            f=list(e);f[k]+=1;f=tuple(f)
            if f not in seen:seen.add(f);todo.append(f)
    std=sorted(std);index={e:i for i,e in enumerate(std)}
    def nfvec(p):
        rem=G.reduce(eval_laurent(p))[1]
        col=[0]*len(std)
        for e,c in s.Poly(rem,*vars).terms():
            if c:col[index[e]]=c
        return col
    expected=sum(ds[i]*ds[j]*abs(det(vs[i],vs[j])) for i in range(len(vs)) for j in range(len(vs)) if i!=j)
    assert len(std)==expected,(len(std),expected)
    vertices=[(sum(t*d*v[0] for t,d,v in zip(signs,ds,vs)),sum(t*d*v[1] for t,d,v in zip(signs,ds,vs))) for signs in itertools.product([-1,1],repeat=len(vs))]
    h=hull(vertices)
    lattice=[(a,b) for a in range(min(p[0] for p in h),max(p[0] for p in h)+1) for b in range(min(p[1] for p in h),max(p[1] for p in h)+1) if inside((a,b),h)]
    mon_rank=s.Matrix.hstack(*(s.Matrix(nfvec({p:1})) for p in lattice)).rank()
    assert mon_rank==expected
    basis=[]
    basis_polynomials=[]
    for i,v in enumerate(vs):
        for j,w in enumerate(vs):
            if i==j:continue
            E=prod([a for k,a in enumerate(aa) if k!=i]+[c for k,c in enumerate(cc) if k!=j])
            for r in reps(v,w):
                for alpha in range(ds[i]):
                    for beta in range(ds[j]):
                        e=(r[0]+alpha*v[0]-beta*w[0],r[1]+alpha*v[1]-beta*w[1])
                        p=mul(E,{e:1})
                        assert all(inside(k,h) for k in p)
                        basis.append(nfvec(p))
                        basis_polynomials.append(str(eval_laurent(p)))
    basis_rank=s.Matrix.hstack(*(s.Matrix(col) for col in basis)).rank()
    assert len(basis)==expected==basis_rank
    out=dict(case=name,vectors=vs,coefficients_low_to_high=coeffs,quotient_dimension=len(std),predicted_dimension=expected,z_minus_z_lattice_points=len(lattice),monomial_rank=mon_rank,constructed_basis_rank=basis_rank,elapsed_seconds=round(time.time()-start,3))
    matrix=s.Matrix.hstack(*(s.Matrix(col) for col in basis))
    determinant=matrix.det(method='domain-ge')
    assert determinant != 0
    certdir=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]/'results'/'certificates'
    certdir.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    cert=dict(case=name,vectors=vs,coefficients_low_to_high=coeffs,variables=['Y1','Y2','I'],specialization={'X1':2,'X2':3},
       inputs=[str(clear(A)),str(clear(C)),str(I*Y1*Y2-1)],
       groebner_order='grevlex',groebner_basis=[str(g.as_expr()) for g in G.polys],
       standard_monomial_exponents=[list(e) for e in std],
       basis_polynomials=basis_polynomials,
       normal_form_matrix=[[str(x) for x in row] for row in matrix.tolist()],
       determinant=str(determinant),
       z_minus_z_lattice_points=[list(p) for p in lattice],predicted_dimension=expected)
    (certdir/(name+'.json')).write_text(json.dumps(cert,indent=2))
    out['determinant_nonzero']=True
    print(json.dumps(out),flush=True)

if __name__=='__main__':
    cases=[
      ('unimodular_two_directions',[(1,0),(0,1)],[[-1,1],[-1,1]]),
```
